title: d-5: storage-contract
description:
## Deliverables
1. Define the one shared sc-storage Storage<T> trait and its single AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) operation for several row operations as one atomic unit; SQLite (d-6), Postgres (d-7) and MySQL (d-8) each implement that same contract (ANC-032/033). Define real std-only sc-storage Storage<T>, generic row/atomic transaction/error contracts and generic test doubles. No consumer table type, schema or SQL is in a backend (ANC-034). Prototype a fresh owned Send+'static future per retry; phase-d transaction properties are name and read-only/read-write (ANC-033); engine retry defaults do not preclude a later transaction-specific retry policy. Preserve measured transaction observations: name, queue wait, run time, row operations and outcome.
2. Freeze row descriptors with validated Identifier values, typed StorageError codes/retryability/source/recovery, and template WidgetStorage/OpenWidgetStore/StoresView extensions preserving existing create/get/delete (REQ-RUN-0201/0328/0330). Public storage functions return typed Results and never panic (ANC-035). Backend factory entry points are concrete inherent methods; sc-command owns Transform and plain storage_read/storage_write functions in d-10, with no StorageCommands or SqliteDatabaseFactory trait.
3. Define CronRow and an intentionally open CronStorage domain interface in sc-cron. CronStore wraps a backend Storage<CronRow>; it does not implement a public raw-write supertrait that bypasses fencing/name/row-limit policy. Declare the one shared generic double and conformance suite; d-9 implements cron policy once and owns its domain suite (REQ-CRON-0004/0005/0020/0021).
4. Register sc-storage and shared SDK/backend dependencies in root/template registries and boundaries including the cron Windows dev-dependency lines, with >= tested floors and no upper bound (ANC-037). Root owns rusqlite >=0.41. Make only the legacy SQLite API/dependency adaptations necessary for this contract branch's workspace build; the named files pass to d-9 for removal after contract sanity. Preserve existing legacy tests. Development remains0.2.0; release is coordinated0.3.0.
5. Amend REQ-RUN-0002/0702 and NFR-RUN-0009 for nine public0.3.0 crates and shared-storage typed errors; amend REQ-DBSQ-0001/0002 for sc-storage/Tokio plus the generic async writer surface; amend REQ-CRON-0001/0004 and NFR-CRON-0001 for sc-storage/sc-command/sc-monty domain policy and removal of direct cron rusqlite/Monty engine ownership. Amend ADR-RUN-0020/0021 with the exact tested contracts. Owner (randlee) ratification of the proposed extension/transaction/row/migration shape is PENDING: record it and change both ADR statuses to Active before this sprint closes or d-6..d-12 start. Synchronization and unspecified permissions remain deferred.
6. Record the existing one-checker interim rule in ADR-RUN-0005: d-3 owns it, d-11 uses it for generation, d-12 for unpacked archives/upload. Consumer=release reviewer; defect=restrictive SDK manifest defaults; remove after equivalent sc-lint#936 release and adoption. Record the approved nine-package tradeoff in ADR-RUN-0020: only SQLite gets the new published engine crate this phase; table-neutral Postgres/MySQL implementations remain generated, so fixes to that generated engine code require template updates/regeneration, not cargo update. Do not claim otherwise.

7. Deliver sc-monty in Wave 1 as the single Monty implementation, beginning with an exact copy of current sc-cron Monty code AND its unit and integration tests, passing before API extension. The exact baseline retains its existing dependencies until its copied unit/integration tests pass at a recorded commit before any API change. Preserve those assertions while separating cron/JSON adapters; at d-5 closure sc-monty production dependencies are only pydantic Monty crates; no sc-*, Tokio, serde_json, cron types or reserved cron names. It owns compilation, compiled sessions, resource limits, host dispatch, typed errors and session byte dump/load. Expose a compiled session and value-level MontyInvoke<Tin,Tout> (script, function name, inputs -> output); no new serialization framework. Move all interpreter machinery here; sc-cron, sc-command and generated services call it and contain no second host. Scheduler-specific adaptation and its integration tests remain in sc-cron, receiving Monty values rather than JSON strings. Register this ninth public crate in workspace/release/boundary inputs with open dependency floors; d-9 consumes it for hooks/cache and d-10 directly for transforms. — owner 2026-11-12 requirement change, item 1 and copy/single-implementation rulings.

## Boundaries and handoffs
No production storage engine or cron policy implementation, generated integration or publication; this sprint does deliver the independent sc-monty interpreter implementation. Real contract types/doubles compile and the workspace builds. Exact new transaction futures are prototype risk, not copied atm-core typed operations. D-6..d-10 consume the closed, ratified contract.
Register tests/support/storage and tests/support/cron-storage as allowed_test_double_paths in the relevant storage/cron boundary manifests and sc-lint configuration; these are private test support. Hand only each specific boundary facade file to d-6/d-9 after contract sanity. Convert sc-cron Windows dev requirements win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0 here; d-9 leaves those lines unchanged (ANC-037).

The real sc-monty crate code and its initial copy/tests close here before d-9/d-10 consume it. Register sc-monty in the template service registry without coupling its feature to cron; hand template service manifests to d-10 and daemon selection to d-11. The cache-specific MontyBlobRow belongs to d-9, not a generic engine.

The REQ/ADR amendments state the following contract, implemented by the named downstream owners: sc-cron captures each compiled session immediately after compilation and before any hook runs, then saves that snapshot through Storage<MontyBlobRow>, keyed by sc-sha SHA-256(source) plus dump version; source in CronRow is authoritative and only a matching key may load. Missing/corrupt/version-incompatible/missing-hook blobs recompile from source and overwrite; schedule writes reject non-compiling source before a tick (d-9; ANC-044/045/046/048). Transform sources load from an app-owned UTF-8 file at invocation and can be replaced without rebuilding (d-10; ANC-049). Transform/storage_read/storage_write are documented as provisional0.3.0 and their signatures preserve later second-input, typed no-write and atomic-transform additions without building those options (ANC-050/051/052). Basic commands need only types, built-in plain conversion and Storage<T>, without an app-written transform/action; no REQ/ADR mandates hand-writing or forbids later consumer-side generation (ANC-056/057/058). Widget create/delete use storage_write and get uses storage_read. The complete cron command set is cron.start/cron.end via storage_write and cron.list via storage_read; none is excluded. Consumers may enrich JSON before schedule persistence (d-11; ANC-053/054/055/059/060/063).

The complete cron command set is: cron.start uses storage_write; cron.end uses storage_write; cron.list uses storage_read. Every cron command uses the shared path. No cron command is excluded (ANC-053/054).
acceptance_criteria:
boundary:storage-contract — Real exported row/storage/transaction/error/extension contracts and generic double compile; tests import production definitions, not replicas. Prototype verifies fresh owned retry bodies, atomic rollback on controlled Pending/error, exactly name/mode properties and controlled-clock transaction observations (ANC-033). Demonstrate multi-row-type support or the tested single-row-type limitation; if neither contract passes atomic/retry/safety cases, closure stays blocked.
boundary:storage-contract/ratification — Record randlee ratification and Active ADR-RUN-0020/0021 with the exact tested shape before closure. The named REQ/NFR amendments match the nine-package0.3.0 architecture. Future consumers never start against merely Proposed ADRs.
boundary:storage-contract/errors — StorageError exposes stable code, retryability, std::error::Error source and recovery guidance; mappings preserve those as typed cause/details without replacing existing domain error codes. Identifier construction returns typed errors and engines quote identifiers/parameterize values; descriptors contain no raw SQL.
boundary:storage-contract/workspace — cargo build --workspace and existing sc-cron legacy SQLite tests pass after necessary inherited rusqlite0.41 adaptations. Retain legacy assertions in the shared conformance suite. Generic test support contains no CronRow or domain policy; sc-storage is std-only.
Required: cargo test -p sc-storage; cargo test --manifest-path tests/support/storage/Cargo.toml; cargo test -p sc-cron; cargo test --manifest-path tests/contracts/storage-v2/Cargo.toml; cargo build --workspace; sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml. The actual sc-lint#931 no-panic and external transaction-body analyzer must exist and pass on changed storage code before closure. Controlled unsafe-await/unmarked-helper/Pending cases stay separate from static proof; no implicit waiver.

boundary:sc-monty — First preserve an exact code/test copy, including existing integration tests, and run it before API extension. Port every existing assertion through extraction; the standalone crate tests exercise compile/invoke, host dispatch, resource errors and dump/load with values. Cron-facing integration assertions run through the shared interpreter in d-9, not a replacement host. cargo test -p sc-monty and its README doctest pass; isolated cargo tree shows production dependencies only on the pydantic Monty crates, with no sc-*, tokio, serde_json, cron types or cron-reserved names. No Monty interpreter implementation remains outside sc-monty after the d-9/d-10 handoffs. Nine public crates release at0.3.0; sc-monty is implemented in Wave 1 and packaged in the first publication wave.

boundary:transaction-extensibility — Retain bounded engine retry defaults. The specification uses the agreed non-exhaustive shape and constructors, with no engine-only retry prohibition; no per-transaction policy or test of that future option is built in phase-d (owner item8; PRD-ENG-6).

boundary:copy-first-tests — Stage1: in an isolated baseline worktree, copy the whole current sc-cron package, including all Monty implementation code, unit/integration tests, fixture data and existing dependency manifest, exactly; retain its current dependencies and crate/import identity. Workspace/path wiring selects the copy at crates/sc-monty, not the original sc-cron tree. Run the copied package tests with the same commands/configurations as the repository runs today, against the copy selected by baseline workspace/path wiring, and obtain the same results as the original. The current sc-lint.toml commands are cargo test -p sc-cron and rustup run 1.96.1 cargo test -p sc-cron --features monty (the baseline retains crate identity sc-cron). Keep current feature gates, skips and ignored tests unchanged; the ignored sc_compose_bench benchmark stays ignored. Normal output shows the copied tests and their results in those existing configurations. Add no checker or new configuration matrix. Record that passing baseline commit before any API change and keep it reachable as an ancestor of the d-5 closing commit, not an orphaned scratch commit. This baseline is not publishable; the old dependency graph is intentional at this stage. Stage2: restore the normal repository workspace with separate sc-cron and sc-monty members while separating the interpreter into sc-monty, retaining every copied assertion. Interpreter assertions run there; scheduler/store/JSON assertions remain with the real sc-cron implementation and are ported in d-9. At d-5 closure, remove every baseline-only normal/build dependency: sc-monty normal/build dependencies are only the pydantic Monty crates, with no sc-*, tokio or serde_json edge (ANC-039). No cron types or cron-reserved names, including cron_tick and cron_stop, and no second scheduler/store implementation remain anywhere in sc-monty source or tests (ANC-040); cron-specific assertions/fixtures live in sc-cron and exercise the shared interpreter. Remove transitional copied scheduler/store fixtures rather than leave a parallel implementation or a dev-dependency cycle. Preserve the exact baseline in Git history; running the original sc-cron code cannot satisfy its copied-code gate (ANC-039/041/042/062; range9 M28).

boundary:production-dependencies — The published crate normal/build graphs forbid ATM and every sc-compose-repository crate except sc-sha. sc-monty is stricter: only pydantic Monty crates as production dependencies; the new allowed sc-sha use is in sc-cron, not the interpreter (ANC-039/061).

dependencies.title: Phase D: shared app storage, channel writer and published consumer migration
dependencies.description:
Phase D makes the SDK easy to adopt and lets consumers choose dependency upgrades. Product intent is PRD v2.0; the release is the owner-selected nine public crates at0.3.0. Generic backends contain no consumer table code. Sprint metadata.owned_paths is the authoritative full file fence; summaries below are navigation only.

| Sprint | Wave | Boundary | Consumed artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| d-3 | 1 | dependency/source compatibility | none; owns the one manifest checker |
| d-4 | 1 | generation tooling | none |
| d-5 | 1 | storage/atomic/row contract + standalone sc-monty | none; owner ratification and Active ADR0020/0021 before consumers |
| d-6 | 2 | SQLite backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-7 | 2 | Postgres backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-8 | 2 | MySQL backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-9 | 2 | cron domain adapter | d-5 production contract and additive legacy build |
| d-10 | 2 | common commands/transforms | d-3 compiled command server/schema/error ABI, d-5 Storage/row contract |
| d-11 | 3 | generated composition | d-3 checker, d-4 tools, d-6/7/8/9/10 code |
| d-12 | 3 | registry migration/release/recommendations | d-3 source/checker, d-4 tools, d-6/9/10 code; d-11 completion checked before upload |

Ten sprints; critical path3, width6. No dependency exists solely because two sprints edit the same manifest. The release and generated-integration sprints prepare in parallel; upload waits for completed generated integration. No implementation dispatch before plan approval.
dependencies.design:
PRD v2.0 governs product scope. sc-storage is std-only; storage/atomic/row traits are the shared contract, with phase-d transaction name/mode properties and room for later per-transaction retry policy. SQLite uses one async queue and one writer thread exclusively owning its sole write-mode connection, queued writes commit together, and replies follow commit. Only the writer runtime uses Runtime::block_on. Readers use blocking_recv without a runtime; async callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes. Consumer rows/schema/migrations stay above generic engines. sc-cron implements its policy once over generic atomic Storage<CronRow> and keeps raw backend mutation out of the CronStore public facade.

D-5 owns contract types, shared registry/boundary definitions, required REQ/ADR amendments and the minimal legacy compatibility build. Its layer-file handoffs are additive contract/legacy artifacts on existing dependencies, not simultaneous same-wave edits. d-9 owns the0.3.0 removal of ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and obsolete SQLite files after those artifacts compile. Root Cargo.toml passes directly from d-5 registrations to d-12 release-version conversion; d-6 reads it. d-3 owns the command manifest with its rmcp3.9 server/schema compatibility code; d-10 consumes that compiled artifact and later adds storage helpers. Specific crate facade boundaries pass from d-5 to their implementation owner on the existing must-follow edges.

D-5 owner ratification is pending and gates its closure; ADR0020/0021 must be Active before d-6..d-12 start. The actual no-panic rule sc-lint#931 and transaction-safe analyzer remain required for affected owner-sprint closure and are rechecked before publication. Lead owns the external analyzer request; missing delivery is a real blocker, not a waiver.

D-3 owns the sole interim SDK manifest checker; d-11 invokes it on generated outputs and d-12 on exact archives/upload. Remove it after equivalent sc-lint#936 release/adoption. Published/template registry requirements are open tested floors (ANC-037); normal tests check the selected versions, with no dedicated min/latest jobs. Consumers may pin what they want. D-12 alone produces the final newest-tested Cargo.lock recommendation and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038).

Nine published packages at0.3.0: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands, sc-monty. Postgres/MySQL generic engines remain generated this phase under that approved packaging scope; their implementation fixes need template updates/regeneration, explicitly recorded in ADR0020. They do not acquire an invented library-upgrade guarantee. D-12 derives publication order from actual manifests, sc-monty/sc-storage in the first wave, rehearses exact archives, then proves actual upstream beads-cache PR open/CI green against registry crates. Its independent preparation does not upload until d-11 sanity is closed and completed composition merged, with ratification and actual safety rules passing. Missing release predicates leave publication open.

The phase is one append-only stack with one writer. Metadata layer is planned presentation order; actual link order follows completion. pr_target is the consumed lower bound, not false sibling serialization. Canonical root Cargo.lock is d-12-owned. Historical probe facts remain in Git/review evidence, not a second live scope document.


## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.

Wave-1 d-5 delivers the single sc-monty implementation, first copying current code and all unit/integration tests exactly and passing them before extension. Its production dependencies are only pydantic Monty crates; sc-cron owns cron/JSON adapters and source-keyed compiled-session blobs via generic Storage rows, sc-sha is permitted. d-11 follows the existing d-9/d-10 prerequisites to route cron.start/end/list through common helpers and a library-owned policy adapter, without bypassing CronStorage or requiring app-written actions. Transform sources load at run time, default conversion needs no hand-written transform, and the provisional0.3.0 seam preserves future second-input/no-write/atomic-transform options without building them.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
1. d-11 closes actual generated SQLite app/cron shared database/channel writer, real typed transforms/CRUD and all selected engines/mixed layouts; no vulnerable SQLx SQLite or separate cron.db default, no fake engine proof.
2. d-12 closes actual upstream migration PR open/CI-green at exact SHA against nine published0.3.0 crates; no path/patch/Git SDK substitute. All source/package/API/docs and normal test suites pass.
3. Generic backends contain no consumer table code; named owned retryable atomic API and static+runtime safety checks actually operate. Public changed storage APIs return typed errors/no panic; writer panic fails every waiting caller. External rule and ratification blockers stay explicit until met.
4. All existing workspace/lint/test/boundary/publishing-kit/controlled-host benchmark gates pass; publication waits for closed d-11 sanity and owner ratification, after exact archive rehearsal. Required coverage and independent plan/development gates are separate from schema validation.
